channel.title: KSL.com - Utah News
channel.description: Utah breaking news and local top stories from KSL.com

item.title: Cambodia's first Latter-day Saint temple opens to the public
item.description: Thirty-two years after missionaries first arrived in Cambodia, the country's first temple of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints is opening its doors to the public.
item.dc:creator: Emma Benson, KSL

item.title: Teen hospitalized with serious injuries after Roy car, e-scooter crash
item.description: A teen was hospitalized with serious injuries in Roy after a crash involving a car and an e-scooter on Wednesday night.
item.dc:creator: Devin Oldroyd, KSL

item.title: 'The future of healthcare': University of Utah opens $215M medical school
item.description: The University of Utah on Wednesday opened the $215 million, state-of-the-art Spencer Fox Eccles School of Medicine in a landmark chapter for the state's only university health system.
item.dc:creator: Logan Stefanich, KSL

item.title: Riverdale man sentenced to up to 15 years imprisonment in sexual abuse case
item.description: A Riverdale man has been sentenced to up to 15 years imprisonment in a sexual abuse case involving a boy.
item.dc:creator: Tim Vandenack, KSL

item.title: Feds officially acknowledge Utah immigrant detention center plans have been abandoned
item.description: In a court filing, federal officials acknowledge that plans for an immigrant detention center in Salt Lake City have been abandoned, which had been presumed.
item.dc:creator: Tim Vandenack, KSL

item.title: Running is really getting their kids somewhere
item.description: Sarah and Sasha Pachev joke that they've got a family farm. But they're not growing corn or raising livestock. They're raising runners.
item.dc:creator: Peter Rosen, KSL

item.title: Utah-based Bricks and Minifigs reaches settlement with family whose allegations went viral
item.description: Wednesday, corporate Bricks and Minifigs announced it and the Mansell family have settled their lawsuits outside of court.
item.dc:creator: Emily Ashcraft, KSL

item.title: UTA considers first base fare rate increase in over a decade
item.description: Utah's largest transit agency is seeking its first base fare increase in over a decade, saying that rising costs are driving up the need.
item.dc:creator: Carter Williams, KSL

item.title: Fire in Uintah brings reminders of 2017 blaze, as firefighters preserve homes
item.description: For some Uintah homeowners, the Dugway fire was a frightening reminder of a 2017 fire in the area that destroyed several homes.
item.dc:creator: Mike Anderson, KSL

item.title: Utah State Hospital needs 'significant' increase in beds, lawmakers told
item.description: The hospital in Provo currently has 378 beds, but hospital leaders said they need many more, starting in 2028.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Woodruff, KSL

item.title: Ogden Valley leaders OK 512.6% tax hike, but Utah Supreme Court still has to weigh in
item.description: Ogden Valley officials narrowly approved a budget plan calling for a 512.6% tax hike, but the Utah Supreme Court still has to weigh in.
item.dc:creator: Tim Vandenack, KSL

item.title: Utah finds a new economic and ecological partner in Argentina
item.description: Utah has a new friend in South America, and the relationship could bring the state significant economic opportunity and answers to its most difficult ecological problems.
item.dc:creator: Eva Terry, Deseret News

item.title: Bats prompt concern ahead of back-to-school at Stansbury Park Elementary School
item.description: As thousands of students prepare to return to classrooms across Utah, staff at Stansbury Park Elementary are working to address an ongoing problem: bats getting inside the school.
item.dc:creator: Garna Mejia, KSL

item.title: 2 Bears Ears guides share differing perspectives on preservation of the surrounding lands
item.description: Two friends who also guide tourists around Bears Ears share their differing visions for protecting the land.
item.dc:creator: Mike Anderson, KSL

item.title: Lehi High School students begin final school year in Alpine School District
item.description: Students at Lehi High School are starting a historic school year as Alpine School District prepares to split into three separate districts, with student leaders encouraging classmates to get involved, make connections and create lasting memories.
item.dc:creator: Madi Vollmer, KSL

item.title: 4 charged in 'long-term investigation' into Utah street gang
item.description: Four gang members recently charged as part of a long-term investigation highlight a recent rash of gang activity in Salt Lake County.
item.dc:creator: Pat Reavy, KSL

item.title: Utah Senate president threatens critics with defamation lawsuits
item.description: Utah Senate President Stuart Adams is threatening several critics with defamation lawsuits for comments made following his primary election defeat in June.
item.dc:creator: Bridger Beal-Cvetko and Daniel Woodruff, KSL

item.title: Moab man dies in Nevada car crash
item.description: A 72-year-old man from Moab was killed after his truck spun out of control while traveling on state Route 305 in Nevada.
item.dc:creator: Joe R. Wirthlin Jr, KSL

item.title: Residents voice concerns over self-powered data center proposal in Spanish Fork
item.description: Dozens of people voiced their concerns and questions about a proposed data center at the mouth of Spanish Fork Canyon in a meeting that stretched past midnight Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Cassidy Wixom and Shelby Lofton, KSL

item.title: Documented gang member faces 26 felony drug and gun-related charges
item.description: A documented gang member was using social media to distribute guns and drugs, according to prosecutors.
item.dc:creator: Pat Reavy, KSL
